### `MlxBindingsContext::apply_compiled_silu`

```rust
pub fn apply_compiled_silu(&self, compiled_elementwise_graphs: &MlxCompiledElementwiseGraphs, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies `input * sigmoid(input)` as one compiled composite.

Stock MLX defines `nn.silu` as a shapeless `mx.compile`, which fuses the sigmoid and the multiply into one kernel reading the input once. The raw two-op composition runs two kernels and roughly 2.5x the memory traffic, which the gated-delta convolution path paid on every layer of every prefill chunk and decode step.

### `MlxBindingsContext::apply_compiled_signed_float32_cast`

```rust
pub fn apply_compiled_signed_float32_cast(&self, compiled_elementwise_graphs: &MlxCompiledElementwiseGraphs, activations: &MlxArray, signs: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies `astype(activations, float32) * signs` as one compiled composite.

The Hadamard-rotated families cast every activation to float32 and flip its signs before the block transform; uncompiled, that is a cast kernel plus a multiply kernel with a float32 intermediate round trip. The fused launch reads the activation once and writes the signed float32 result once, with arithmetic identical to the two-op chain.

### `MlxBindingsContext::apply_compiled_softplus`

```rust
pub fn apply_compiled_softplus(&self, compiled_elementwise_graphs: &MlxCompiledElementwiseGraphs, input: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies the K2 Horizon MoVA softplus gate as one compiled composite.

The gate formula is `log1p(exp(input * ln2)) / ln2` — the reference implementation's beta-scaled softplus, which is NOT the standard `logaddexp(input, 0)` softplus and must not be "simplified" to it. Compiling collapses the four hand-composed dispatches into one launch without changing the arithmetic.

### `MlxBindingsContext::apply_compiled_vision_rope`

```rust
pub fn apply_compiled_vision_rope(&self, compiled_elementwise_graphs: &MlxCompiledElementwiseGraphs, attention_states: &MlxArray, rotary_cosines: &MlxArray, rotary_sines: &MlxArray, first_half: &MlxArray, second_half: &MlxArray) -> Result<MlxArray, MlxCError>
```

Applies Qwen3-VL rotate-half rotary embedding as one compiled composite.

`first_half` and `second_half` are the pre-sliced head halves of `attention_states` (the last axis split at `head_dim / 2`); the head-half slices stay outside the compiled graph because the pinned MLX `Slice` primitive cannot be shapeless-compiled. The remaining composite fuses the elementwise tail into one kernel and keeps the rotate-half concat as one shape kernel, replacing the eight separate dispatches.

## `src/compile/gated_delta_rate_activation.rs`

Dual-output compiled composite for the gated-delta rate activations.

The sigmoid over the update logits and the complete decay formula both consume the two pre-activations of the fused rate projection, and each ran as its own launch in every gated-delta layer of every decode step. One multi-output compiled replay produces both, reading each input once. The per-element arithmetic is the same primitive sequence the two separate launches ran — sigmoid untouched, and the decay chain identical to `crate::compile::elementwise_graphs`'s single-output graph — so the replay matches the composed path bit for bit. Decode speed is bound by launches per token, and this removes one launch from every gated-delta layer.

Output order is fixed by the builder: the sigmoid update rates first, the decay factors second. Callers consume them by that order.


### `set_graph_output`

```rust
pub unsafe fn set_graph_output(output_vector: *mut raw::mlx_vector_array, graph_output: &MlxArray) -> c_int
```

Publishes the single output of a single-output graph builder.

**Safety:** The caller must guarantee that `output_vector` is unique, live, and a valid `mlx_vector_array` destination for the whole call.

### `set_graph_output_vector`

```rust
pub unsafe fn set_graph_output_vector(output_vector: *mut raw::mlx_vector_array, graph_outputs: &[&MlxArray]) -> c_int
```

Publishes a multi-output graph's complete ordered result vector at once.

Compiled-graph tracing hands builders an output vector whose context may still be null, and MLX's append operation throws on that null context while its whole-vector set allocates on demand; collecting the outputs locally and publishing them once at the end of the builder is therefore the only trace-safe multi-output pattern.

**Safety:** The caller must guarantee that `output_vector` is unique, live, and a valid `mlx_vector_array` destination for the whole call.

## `src/compile/multi_output_graph.rs`

### `MlxCompiledMultiOutputGraph`

```rust
pub struct MlxCompiledMultiOutputGraph
```

Owns one compiled MLX graph that produces an ordered vector of outputs.

Model-side compiled composites that need several outputs at once — the multi-token-prediction verification window returns successor states beside its logits — construct one of these with their own graph builder and apply it through `MlxBindingsContext::apply_compiled_multi_output_graph`. Output order is the builder's write order and never changes after compilation.

## `src/compile/norm_fusion.rs`

Epsilon-specialized compiled composite fusing the gated-delta head normalizations.

The query/key head RMS normalizations of the gated-delta prework ran as two launches per layer; one dual-output replay produces both. Every primitive and its order match the composed path — `mlx_fast_rms_norm` is the identical Metal kernel over its own input — so the results do not change. This matters because decode speed is bound by launches per token.

A second fusion was tried here and rejected by the trajectory replay: chaining the output RMS normalization into the precise SwiGLU epilogue passed synthetic bit parity at small widths yet diverged the real upstream trajectory, because MLX's compiler reshapes the reduction schedule when the elementwise epilogue is fused at the model's real widths. Reduction-into-epilogue fusions stay composed until a kernel-level contract can pin the summation order.

Graph builders are plain function pointers that cannot capture the RMS epsilon, and `mlx_fast_rms_norm` bakes its epsilon into the compiled graph at trace time, so the epsilon rides in a process-wide bit slot for the duration of each compilation. Model loads are sequential in a worker process — one resident model at a time — which is the contract that keeps the slot race-free; the compiled graphs keep their baked value forever and later slot writes cannot affect them.


Traces a closure for the VMAP transform, producing traced inputs and outputs. `MlxClosure::vmapped` is the whole transform; this and `vmap_replace` are its two building blocks.


Vectorizes this closure: arguments map over `input_axes` and outputs stack along `output_axes`. An empty list means axis 0 throughout.

**Errors:** Returns the captured MLX-C description when the transform fails.
